name: KASKA
summary: KASKA was a Japanese near/far reactor-antineutrino proposal to measure theta13 at the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power station. It developed detector and underground-site designs during the 2000s but did not become an operating theta13 experiment.
detection_principle: Matched gadolinium-loaded scintillator detectors would detect inverse beta decay at near and far baselines. Relative event rates and spectra would isolate disappearance while cancelling reactor and detector systematics.

status.label: Historical proposal / not realized
status.evidence: The 2009 reactor-programme overview identifies KASKA among the historical proposals that did not proceed to the running theta13 programme.

timeline.event: Letter of intent and underground-background studies released
Later programme overview records it as an unrealized historical proposal

key_parameters.name: Proposed configuration
key_parameters.value: Four identical detectors: two near and two far

key_parameters.name: Reactor complex
key_parameters.value: Seven reactors, 24.3 GW thermal total in the proposal

results.summary: The design established projected theta13 sensitivity; it produced no full-scale reactor-oscillation measurement.
